chunks: Sa'd, from Abi Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abī Ja'far عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who joined a group, while he himself had not prayed al-ẓuhr, and the people were praying al-'aṣr,
He عليه السلام said: “He makes the prayer that he performed with them as al-ẓuhr, and then afterward he himself prays al-'aṣr.”

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the noon prayer, which remains due upon him
key_terms.الْعَصْرَ: the afternoon prayer being performed by the congregation
key_terms.بَعْدُ: afterward; indicating the sequence of prayers
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the individual asking about or described in the ruling
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his prayer, as designated by intention

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he joins a congregation praying al-'aṣr before he has prayed al-ẓuhr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for someone who joins a congregation praying al-'aṣr while he has not yet performed al-ẓuhr. He should join them, count that prayer as al-ẓuhr for himself, and then pray al-'aṣr afterward.
